In the "cliff walking" example, Q-Learning learns the optimal path right along the edge of the cliff, though it often falls during the learning process due to exploration [Source 4]. Sarsa learns a safer path further from the cliff because it accounts for the possibility of making a random move [Source 4]. As a result, Sarsa typically collects a higher sum of rewards during training, whereas Q-Learning finds a better final path if exploration is disabled [Source 5].
